title: Open in Terminal allows shell command substitution from filenames
reasoning: The selected path is interpolated into a Terminal command as cd "..." after only backslashes and double quotes are escaped. Shell double quotes still evaluate command substitutions such as $() and backticks, so opening Terminal in a directory whose name contains command substitution can execute arbitrary shell commands under the user's account.
reproduction: Create or select a folder named $(touch /tmp/grove-terminal-pwn), choose Open in Terminal, and the generated Terminal command will evaluate the substitution before cd runs.
recommendation: Build the Terminal command using a real shell-quoted path, for example AppleScript's quoted form of the POSIX path, and keep AppleScript string escaping separate from shell escaping.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this controller feature, and this requires a malicious filesystem-name case through the context-menu Terminal action.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test around the script/command builder with paths containing $(), backticks, quotes, spaces, and apostrophes, asserting the generated command cannot perform shell substitution.
minimumFixScope: Change FileListViewController.contextOpenInTerminal path quoting or extract a safe command builder used by that action.

history.reasoning: Original evidence path still exists, but the vulnerable code has moved/changed. Current Grove/Controllers/FileListViewController.swift:1625-1658 routes Open in Terminal through terminalChangeDirectoryScript(for:), builds command = "cd \(shellQuotedPath(url.path))", and shellQuotedPath wraps the path in single quotes while escaping embedded single quotes as '\'' before AppleScript string escaping. That prevents $() and backticks from being evaluated by the shell. A repository search found no other Swift do-script cd path interpolation. GroveTests/BrowserCapabilityTests.swift:35-43 now includes a regression test for paths containing $(), backticks, and single quotes. Focused xcodebuild test could not execute in this read-only sandbox because xcodebuild could not create /tmp xcrun/cache/result-bundle files, but current code and test evidence indicate the finding is fixed.
